{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting / Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable to us and, in several respects, better than our preferred position: there is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN burden, no liquidated damages or exit fee, and no audit right running against us. Section 2(a) expressly preserves our freedom to acquire, develop or license competing software and services, and Section 6 caps Hosting Services price increases for the first year and benchmarks rates to TrueLink's best customer pricing. Our termination-for-convenience right under Section 14 is unilateral, penalty-free and effective within roughly 30–60 days, and the Section 13 auto-renewal (one-year terms, 30 days' non-renewal notice) sits at our preferred position.

The risk is concentrated in the protections that are simply absent. There are seven deviations or gaps, all of the "nothing was drafted for our benefit" type:

- **Liability is asymmetric.** The only limitation caps TrueLink at 12 months' hosting and support compensation while our liability — including the broad Section 12(a) indemnity — is uncapped. That is express walk-away territory under our playbook, and there is no mutual consequential-damages exclusion anywhere in the document.
- **No vendor indemnity for IP infringement.** TrueLink's Section 12(b) indemnity covers only its own breach; all infringement risk runs against us.
- **No performance warranty.** The only vendor warranty is a Y2K date-handling warranty; hosting obligations are "reasonable commercial efforts" with no remedy.
- **No exit rights over our own data.** There is no data return, migration assistance or certified deletion obligation; Section 13 places the entire re-hosting burden on us.
- **No insurance requirement at all**, for a vendor that hosts our Web Site, holds Client Content and transmits data under Credit Repository Agreements.
- **Ownership of Support Services work product and our borrower/loan data is unaddressed**, and Section 15 assignment has no successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard on consent.

We recommend treating the liability cap, the vendor indemnity and the data-exit package as gating items.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | Non-exclusive licence; Section 2(a) confirms we are not obligated to use the licence and may buy or build competing products. Section 3(i) is a narrow self-triggered operational term, not a sole-source covenant. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No liquidated damages, penalty or exit fee. Section 14 wind-down is roughly one further month of fees. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE | No field-of-use or non-compete restraint on us; Section 8(d)'s reference to a separate Non-Competition Agreement limits TrueLink's use of Credit Data (in our favour) — diligence item only. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | Section 14 gives us a unilateral, penalty-free at-will right (~30–60 days). TrueLink has no mid-term convenience exit. No express pro-rata refund, but fees are billed monthly in arrears, so immaterial. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | No audit or inspection right against us; verification rights under §§ 5–6 run in our favour. We should not introduce one. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY | Sections 26–27 select California law with exclusive venue in San Luis Obispo County. Sits at the fallback (California accepted, courts not arbitration); vendor-home-county venue noted, not flagged. |
| Medium | **LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY | TrueLink capped at 12 months' hosting/support fees (and only as to Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11); our liability, including the § 12(a) indemnity, is uncapped. No mutual consequential-damages exclusion; no Excluded Claims. Fails the fallback. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION | The only MFN language runs in our favour (TrueLink's Hosting rates not to exceed those charged to any other party). |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION | § 5(a) monthly minimum, but confined to a single 12-month term and exitable under § 14; no shortfall or take-or-pay. Commercial points: minimum amounts are blank ($____) and § 6 excludes minimums from our documentation/dispute rights. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 7 UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL E-MAIL | No non-solicit, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on us. Separate Non-Competition Agreement to be reviewed for personnel restrictions. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 13: successive one-year renewals, 30 days' notice by either party — both parameters at preferred. No renewal reminder and no renewal price cap; § 6 partially mitigates. |
| Medium | **TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return** | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY | No data return, migration assistance or deletion obligation. § 13 puts the name-server (30 days) and hosting (60 days) burden on us; § 10 has no return-or-destroy mechanic. Below the fallback. |
| Medium | **WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration** | **Deviation** | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only vendor warranty is the § 9 Y2K warranty. No professional-and-workmanlike, conformance, malicious-code or compliance warranty and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy; § 3 is "reasonable commercial efforts" only. The general disclaimer is acceptable as it is qualified by "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT." |
| Low | **ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 15 bars assignment absent consent, with a carve-out only for a financially responsible affiliate. No successor/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction. No CoC-triggered vendor termination or re-pricing, so not walk-away. |
| Low | **INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor** | **Deviation** | § 12 INDEMNITY | § 12(b) covers only TrueLink's own breach or performance failure. No IP infringement indemnity anywhere; the only infringement language runs against us. Compounded by the broad § 12(a) Client indemnity. |
| Low | **INSURANCE — Vendor insurance** | **Missing** | § 12 INDEMNITY | No insurance provision at all. TrueLink hosts our Web Site, holds Client Content and transmits data under Credit Repository Agreements. Neither preferred nor fallback limits met. |
| Low | **IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data** | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE | § 2(d) reserves the Interface to TrueLink (acceptable), but nothing vests us with ownership of § 4 Support Services work product or our borrower/loan data, and there is no licence-back of embedded TrueLink IP. Confidentiality treatment under § 10(b)/(c) is not ownership. § 8(d) Credit Data licence left intact. |
| Low | **LICENSE — Licence grant scope** | **Deviation** | § 2 LICENSE | § 2(a) licenses Client alone; no affiliates or contractors, and § 2(b) permits added sites only, not added entities. § 15 allows transfer only to a financially responsible affiliate, not an M&A successor. Fails both limbs of the fallback; not revocable at will, so not walk-away. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Uncapped Customer liability against a capped Vendor (LOL-CAP, § 12 INDEMNITY).** Our liability, including the broad § 12(a) indemnity, is uncapped while TrueLink is capped at 12 months' hosting and support compensation. Our playbook treats this expressly as walk-away. We require a mutual, agreement-wide cap set at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential damages, standard uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirmation that our payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.
2. **No contractual right to our own hosted data on exit (TRANSITION, § 12 INDEMNITY).** With no return, export or deletion obligation, on termination we would have no contractual route to the data TrueLink holds. Our position is transition assistance for 6 months at then-current rates, return within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter (fallback: 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days).
3. **No vendor insurance for a vendor processing our data (INSURANCE, § 12 INDEMNITY).** This is the rule's identified walk-away case. We require CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M and workers' compensation with certificates on request; fallback E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M.

We would also treat the absence of any Vendor IP infringement indemnity (INDEMN) as effectively non-negotiable given that all infringement risk currently sits with us.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline on the seven open items** — LOL-CAP, TRANSITION, WARRANTY, INDEMN, INSURANCE, IP and LICENSE/ASSIGN — sequenced so that liability, indemnity and data exit are presented as gating and the balance as clean-up:
   - LOL-CAP: mutual, agreement-wide cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, plus consequential-damages exclusion and Excluded Claims.
   - TRANSITION: insert transition assistance, data return within 30 days and certified deletion into Section 14.
   - WARRANTY: insert a TrueLink performance and conformance warranty with repair, replacement and refund remedies.
   - INDEMN: insert a TrueLink IP infringement indemnity with standard exclusions, remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, leaving the Client-side indemnity untouched.
   - INSURANCE: new Section 31 with the coverages above, offering the fallback limits in the comment.
   - IP: Client-ownership paragraph for Support Services results, retention of Client Content, IP and borrower data, licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP, and no joint ownership.
   - LICENSE / ASSIGN: extend the grant to Client affiliates and contractors on written notice; add a mutual successor/M&A carve-out to Section 15, a reasonableness standard and a competitor bar on TrueLink assignments, and confirm a Client change of control is not an assignment.
2. **Counsel to hand-draft the LOL-CAP and TRANSITION language before it goes out.** The automated proposals for these two items did not pass verification, so the clauses should be drafted and proofed manually against Sections 12, 13 and 14 rather than inserted as generated.
3. **Close the blank commercial terms.** Section 5(a) leaves the minimum monthly Hosting and Support fees as "$____". Business team to populate at or below expected usage before signature, and to consider whether Section 6 should stop excluding the monthly minimums from our supporting-documentation and dispute rights.
4. **Obtain and review the separate Non-Competition Agreement** cross-referenced at Section 8(d), specifically for any restriction on our operations or on hiring TrueLink personnel. It is outside this document and has not been reviewed.
5. **Do not introduce protections we do not currently owe.** There is no audit right, no MFN burden, no non-solicit and no exclusivity running against us; we should resist any reciprocal drafting that adds them in response to our requests.
6. **Venue** — California law is acceptable at our fallback. If we have leverage in the final round, we may ask for a neutral California forum rather than TrueLink's home county, but this is not a condition of signature."}
